<meta>This page continues Chapter 5 of the Book of Daniel, following the appearance of the mysterious handwriting on the wall during Belshazzar’s feast. The previous page ended with the King calling for his wise men after being terrified by the supernatural event.</meta>

# Daniel * 5 *
<page-num>1196</page-num>

the King and said to the wise men of Babylon, "Any man who reads this writing and shows me its interpretation shall be
clothed in <term>purple</term><note>A color reserved for royalty and high-ranking officials due to the extreme expense of the dye.</note> and have a necklace of gold around his neck, and shall rule as third in the kingdom."
٨ * Then all the King's wise men entered, but they were not able to read the writing, nor to
٩ make known the interpretation to the King. * Then King Belshazzar was greatly terrified, and his appearance was changed,
١٠ and his nobles were troubled. * As for the Queen, because of the words of the King and his nobles, she entered
the banquet hall; and the Queen answered and said, "O King, live forever.
١١ Do not let your thoughts terrify you, nor let your appearance change. * There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the
holy gods. In the days of your father, light and understanding and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him;
and King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, made him chief of the <term>magi</term>, sorcerers, <term>Chaldeans</term><note>In this context, a class of learned scholars and astrologers in Babylon.</note>, and astrologers.
١٢ Your father the King [did this] * because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, the interpreting of dreams, the explaining
of riddles, and the solving of riddles were found in this Daniel, whom the King named Belteshazzar.

->Let Daniel be called now, and he will show the interpretation<-

١٣ Then Daniel was brought in before the King. And the King answered and said to Daniel,
"Are you that Daniel, one of the captives of Judah, whom my father the King brought from Judah?
١٤ * I have heard of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light, understanding, and excellent
١٥ wisdom are found in you. * And now the wise men and sorcerers were brought before me to read this writing and make known
١٦ to me its interpretation, but they could not show the interpretation of the words. * And I have heard of you,
that you are able to give interpretations and solve riddles. Now if you are able to read
the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed in purple and have a necklace of gold around your neck,
and shall rule as third in the kingdom."
١٧ Then Daniel answered and said before the King, "Let your gifts be for yourself, and give
١٨ your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the King and make known to him the interpretation. * As for you, O
King, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a kingdom, greatness, glory, and majesty.

<meta>This page transitions from the conclusion of a previous set of questions to a new series based on Aristotle’s "De Caelo" (On the Heavens). It marks the beginning of the First and Second Questions regarding optical properties and the natural motion of the four elements.</meta>

From the book "On the Heavens" <note>original: "Kitab al-Sama'," referring to Aristotle's treatise "De Caelo," which discusses the nature of the universe and the four elements.</note> regarding Aristotle, he began the response to the other questions with the permission of God the Almighty.

**The First Question**

If there is a clear, white, spherical glass vessel filled with clear water, it takes the place of a spherical crystal in causing combustion <term>al-ihraq</term> <note>the focused point of heat produced by a lens or burning-sphere.</note>. If the vessel is empty of clear water and contains only air, it does not cause burning and does not collect the light rays. Why does water perform this action while air does not? And why does this burning and the collection of rays occur?

**The Answer**

Water is a dense, heavy body that possesses a slight color in its essence. The denser a body is, the more light reflects from it. Therefore, the light reflects from the glass <margin>which is densely packed</margin> when it is filled with water. A strong burning occurs as a result of this powerful reflection <note>Though the author uses the term "reflection" (in’ikas), the phenomenon described is refraction. Medieval scientists often viewed the bending of light through a dense medium as a form of redirection or reflection toward a central point.</note>. As for air, it is not a substance from which light reflects, nor does light reflect within it, because air is truly transparent. Therefore, if there is air in the glass, no strong reflection occurs from it.

**The Second Question**

Which of these two views is correct? One speaker says that water and earth move toward the center, while air and fire move away from the center. Another says <margin>among them</margin> that all the elements move toward the center, but the heaviest of them simply precedes the lightest in its movement toward it.

**The Answer**

The statement of the second opponent is false. If fire moved toward the center, it would either reach the center during its motion or it would never reach it. If it never reaches it, then it is not truly moving toward it.

<summary>This page addresses why water-filled glass spheres can focus light to start fires while air-filled ones cannot, and debates whether all elements naturally move toward the center of the universe.</summary>
<keywords>Aristotle, De Caelo, optics, combustion, elements, natural motion, reflection, refraction</keywords>

Long nails are beautiful on the hand and, when seen, are captivating to the minds of women; these are generally for the Gaudas. <note>9</note>

In terms of measurement, there are three types. "Long"—those that have the habit of adorning the hand; they are unable to perform [precise] nail-cutting. "Captivating to the mind when seen"—these possess two qualities, as they are mostly for touching, generally used by the Gaudas. <note>9</note>

"With them"—with medium nails, all five. "Well-adjusted"—well-connected. This statement is in relation to a medium state. translation:
<header>Fifth Chapter</header>

Root Text—Whoever treats this moving and unmoving world as indirect, and abandons the direct Supreme <term>Brahman</term> <gloss>the Absolute</gloss>, dissolves into that which is abandoned. || 222 ||

Commentary—People who, by arguing through scriptures, treat this world of the moving and unmoving as indirect, and abandon the direct Supreme <term>Brahman</term> <gloss>the Absolute</gloss>—meaning they do not even attain <term>Brahman</term>—these ignorant ones dissolve into the world; that is, they do not attain liberation. || 222 ||

Root Text—So that the ignorance, which is the cause of knowledge, does not arise repeatedly, the yogi should always practice, free from associations. || 223 ||

Commentary—The yogi should always practice this yoga, free from associations, by which knowledge arises and ignorance is destroyed. || 223 ||

Root Text—Having restrained all senses from the objects, the wise one should remain, free from associations, in the rejection of objects, just like one in deep sleep. || 224 ||

Commentary—The wise yogi, having stopped the senses from objects and remaining free from associations, should stay steady in the renunciation of objects, just like one in deep sleep. || 224 ||

translation:
Al-Hasan, then Al-Husayn, the Prophet completes Al-Husayn.
Their light is like their names, their grandfather is upon him.
Follow them, pray upon him, the prayers of God be upon him.
And everyone who greets him receives the blessing of God.
Whoever may be for me, from you, in pain, O God of the Kohl-lined eye,
May they be kind, and my love has believed in him, and you know of my state.
It is not ephemeral, and may he pray upon him, my soul is a ransom for my master.
O my beloved, O Messenger, O intercessor for the sinners.
O God, bless and grant peace to our master Muhammad and those who followed him,
All of them, with a prayer and peace that may be your light of satisfaction, and to him
Belongs the reward for his right, performing it upon the saints, a secret and proof, understanding it by him in
My secret and my proclamation, and those who were intoxicated, what was Yā-Sīn <note>referring to the chapter of the Quran</note>, so it became clear with the protection of the intoxicated.
Love from your generosity and my knowledge, if I were before the seizing, then I would seek.
A majesty that wanders between the worlds, and God gave me, I am the pearl of the white ones.
I am the lotus tree of satisfaction and a path, and the encompassing of the Beloved, and call me.



And the revelation of the veils from a light and its glory, and from the redness of the orientation
And the nearness he gave me to drink, the gaze of the Throne upon him, and his gaze, so it appeared.
In the kingdom of God, and God named me, and if I, when the dome traveled with them in a lake,
It would overflow, and they were angry from my traveling and my proof, and if I, when the dome traveled,
Upon the misguided, the Ahmad-like fires, from one of great authority, and likewise,
The pole of the Gospel, I gathered them all, and I interpreted in the letter Nun a part of my knowledge.
And a sphere, a symbol that was difficult to carry, he was the giver of life to the dead, and a Syriac symbol.
And likewise, the Waj <note>referring to the Divine Essence</note> name, I understood them all, the entirety of the Psalms, then my Quran.
So who is like me, and who is my second? For I am the grandfather of the Messenger of God, and the origin saw me.
I am the pole of the time, Abd al-Qadir, and my name is Muhibb al-Din, and my origin is Gilani.
And every pole and sheikh is beneath my feet; I am beneath the feet of the Prophet, like the pattern.
My perfection is like the stars in the heaven and the earth, and it tasted, so come forward, O seeker.
Do not fear, God is my Lord; I am the lofty Qadir over the heights, and every pole and sheikh
Circumambulates the House <note>the Kaaba</note> seven times, and I am in the House with my cup. Sheikh of God,
Sultan of the time, Sheikh Malik al-Yaman, O Sultan Safi al-Din al-Ahmad ibn Alwan.

And morning overtook Shahrazad, so she fell silent.

<center>The One Thousand and Seventh Night</center>

When the next night arrived, she said, "O auspicious King, the Queen said to the King, 'O my cousin, do not think that you love me, for I have attained your companionship.' When he heard her words and she was drunk, there was hidden in his soul what she had prepared for him. She tempted him and showed him love, and she slept beside him. When it was midnight, he rose from the bed, and King Badr was aware of her, but he pretended to be asleep. He opened one eye to see what she was doing. He found that she had taken out a bag of red earth and spread it in the middle of the palace. It became a flowing river. She took a handful of barley and scattered it on the earth, watering it with that water, so it became crops just as she had taken it. She harvested it and ground it, and it became flour. Then she asked him, and she came to the side and slept until morning. When morning came, King Badr got up and did his best to get permission from the Queen to go to the Elder. She gave him permission, so he went to the Elder and told him what he had seen from her. When the Elder heard that, he laughed and said, 'She has betrayed you, by God, this infidel, but do not honor her.' Then he brought him a pound of flour and said, 'Take this with you. When you come to her and she sees this flour with you and asks where you are going, say, "Adding good to good." Eat from it, and if she eats from it, she will offer you her flour, and if she tells you to eat of this flour, show her that you have eaten of it. Eat from this, but do not eat anything of her flour, for if she wants you to, she will deceive you. If she is convinced that you have eaten of her flour, she will move and tell you to "Exit from the natural form to the form you want." She will do the work if you eat from her flour, and if you do not eat, she will not think of you. Her magic will reveal the truth as it really is for you, and she will say to you, "I have returned...""

<summary>The Elder warns Badr about the Queen's magical flour and instructs him on how to trick her into revealing her true nature.</summary>

(A) But it is necessary to awaken the doubt and the rotation of the wheel so that it will be turned according to the world in which it is, for it is in the middle of the third of the West, that the wheel will be turned according to the unfolding action. And this is: "He will turn in His schemes" <note>a reference to Proverbs 12:2, usually read "with his schemes/devices"</note>, written as deficient. And this is in the middle of the third of the West, that the wheel lacks the "Zayin" <note>the letter Z</note> (like writing "action" without the "Vav" according to the laws of language). 

There is in His Name the secret of the "Yod-Heh" <note>the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>, and in His hand is a measuring cord, and with it He measures the length and the breadth of every creature. And every creature is measured according to the laws of language, for the laws of language, etc., and this is in the middle of the third of the West, and it is written "action" deficient there, "action" deficient, etc. And this is "Strength and majesty for Him," for the root of the high is in the level of the straight man. It was not standing in it, and we were never the wheel to be above the language, for there it turns and returns, and in the future, it will be elevated higher and higher. And this is: "Because he departed from there, Abraham," in that which is in the Name that unfolds in it, in the beginning from the dismantling in the middle of the West. It is in the middle of the third, and this is: "These and these are the words of the living God," and this is "this very day," as it is said, "Every day," the unfolding says to say to the time. And in the future, it is written: "On that day, the Lord will be one and His Name One," and it will be in a high level. And this is to Him, blessed be His Name, and this is above, and this is: "And we will bless Yah from now and forever, Hallelujah," for the revelation of the light in the world, etc. 

And this is according to the laws of language without a "Vav," and this is written "in His schemes" deficient. And this is "They are one language," and this is "one language" above, and this is "A language of truth will be established forever," and this is that the light is in the expansion of the Name, meaning deficient. And this is in the aspect of the Name stronger than the light of the light of grace above, that shines to him with a strong light below; also in this, there will be power with him. And this is, etc. And this is in the Midrash, Genesis, chapter 24, etc. And then he has a measuring cord, and with it He created all the heavens and the earth, etc. And in this light, he has strength and power at every moment, with will and from mercy in grace. And this is the aspect: "And His mercies are on all His works." And this is "in His schemes," not this, in the Name "Yod-Heh." And this is in the middle of "schemes" it will fall upon, and wisdom in a multitude of counselors, etc., in the language in this, etc.

And his intention is not to understand and to involve himself in the "Work of the Chariot" <note>the highest form of Jewish mysticism</note>. And Maimonides wrote that anyone who knows how to unify schemes against the inclination, the scheme is good for him in the wicked. He said, "Man and his internal powers, that he will ascend in a multitude of counselors, wisdom is good for him." And this is "scheme" is the essence in this. And this is "Counsel in the heart of man," for schemes and thought in the heart of man, etc., etc. And with the will of two laws of language, etc. "Through schemes you shall make yourself war," and this is the secret of "He will turn in His schemes," this is the workers in Him, and this is language in the aspect of "one language."

<summary>This page discusses the esoteric significance of divine schemes and the "laws of language" in the creation and governance of the world, emphasizing the internal struggle against the inclination through wisdom and divine counsel.</summary>
<keywords>Unfolding, Schemes, Laws of language, Work of the Chariot, Maimonides, Wisdom/Counsel</keywords>

### Emor Translation

...your souls: in the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, shall you celebrate your sabbath.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, saying: The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles <term>Sukkot</term> <gloss>Booths/Tabernacles</gloss> for seven days to the Lord. On the first day shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no servile work therein. Seven days you shall offer an offering made by fire to the Lord. On the eighth day shall be a holy convocation to you; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to the Lord; it is a solemn assembly; and you shall do no servile work therein. These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to offer an offering made by fire to the Lord, a burnt offering, and a meal offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, everything upon its day; beside the sabbaths of the Lord, and beside your gifts, and beside all your vows, and beside all your freewill offerings, which you give to the Lord. Also in the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the fruit of the land, you shall keep a feast to the Lord seven days; on the first day shall be a sabbath, and on the eighth day shall be a sabbath. And you shall take you on the first day the fruit of goodly trees <note>traditionally interpreted as the etrog (citron)</note>, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days. And you shall keep it a feast to the Lord seven days in the year. It shall be a statute forever in your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month. You shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are home-born in Israel shall dwell in booths.

<column-break/>

...that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. And Moses declared to the children of Israel the feasts of the Lord.

<summary>This page outlines the laws for the festival of Sukkot, including the gathering of the four species and the command to dwell in booths to commemorate the exodus from Egypt.</summary>

### קמט
הַלְלוּיָהּ שִׁירוּ לַיהוָה שִׁיר חָדָשׁ תְּהִלָּתוֹ בִּקְהַל חֲסִידִים׃ יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֹשָׂיו בְּנֵי צִיּוֹן יָגִילוּ בְמַלְכָּם׃ יְהַלְלוּ שְׁמוֹ בְמָחוֹל בְּתֹף וְכִנּוֹר יְזַמְּרוּ־לוֹ׃ כִּי־רוֹצֶה יְהוָה בְּעַמּוֹ יְפָאֵר עֲנָוִים בִּישׁוּעָה׃ יַעְלְזוּ חֲסִידִים בְּכָבוֹד יְרַנְּנוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָם׃ רוֹמְמוֹת אֵל בִּגְרוֹנָם וְחֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת בְּיָדָם׃ לַעֲשׂוֹת נְקָמָה בַּגּוֹיִם

<column-break/>

תּוֹכֵחוֹת בַּלְאֻמִּים׃ לֶאְסֹר מַלְכֵיהֶם בְּזִקִּים וְנִכְבְּדֵיהֶם בְּכַבְלֵי בַרְזֶל׃ לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּהֶם מִשְׁפָּט כָּתוּב הָדָר הוּא לְכָל־חֲסִידָיו הַלְלוּ־יָהּ׃

### קנ
הַלְלוּיָהּ הַלְלוּ־אֵל בְּקָדְשׁוֹ הַלְלוּהוּ בִּרְקִיעַ עֻזּוֹ׃ הַלְלוּהוּ בִגְבוּרֹתָיו הַלְלוּהוּ כְּרֹב גֻּדְלוֹ׃ הַלְלוּהוּ בְּתֵקַע שׁוֹפָר הַלְלוּהוּ בְּנֵבֶל וְכִנּוֹר׃ הַלְלוּהוּ בְתֹף וּמָחוֹל הַלְלוּהוּ בְּמִנִּים וְעוּגָב׃ הַלְלוּהוּ בְצִלְצְלֵי־שָׁמַע הַלְלוּהוּ בְּצִלְצְלֵי תְרוּעָה׃ כֹּל הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּל יָהּ הַלְלוּיָהּ׃

translation:
He has made a decree which shall not pass. Praise the Lord from the earth, you sea monsters, and all deeps; fire and hail, snow and vapor; stormy wind, fulfilling His word; mountains and all hills; fruitful trees and all cedars; beasts and all cattle; creeping things and flying fowl; kings of the earth and all peoples; princes and all judges of the earth; both young men and maidens; old men and children. Let them praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted; His glory is above the earth and heaven. He also has lifted up the horn of His people, a praise for all His pious ones, even for the children of Israel, a people near to Him. Hallelujah.

### 149
Hallelujah. Sing to the Lord a new song, His praise in the assembly of the pious. Let Israel rejoice in his Maker; let the children of Zion be joyful in their King. Let them praise His name in the dance; let them sing praises to Him with the timbrel and harp. For the Lord takes pleasure in His people; He will beautify the humble with salvation. Let the pious exult in glory; let them sing for joy upon their beds. Let the high praises of God be in their throat, and a two-edged sword in their hand; to execute vengeance on the nations,
<column-break/>
and punishments on the peoples; to bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron; to execute upon them the judgment written; He is the glory of all His pious ones. Hallelujah.

### 150
Hallelujah. Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in the firmament of His power. Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to His abundant greatness. Praise Him with the blast of the horn; praise Him with the lute and harp. Praise Him with the timbrel and dance; praise Him with stringed instruments and the pipe. Praise Him with the loud-sounding cymbals; praise Him with the clashing cymbals. Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. Hallelujah.

# ❖ Order of the High Priest's Service on the Day of Atonement ❖

**Upon his coming out**, they brought him the goat, the sin-offering of the Name. He slaughtered it and received its blood in a pure basin. He shall enter within to sprinkle from its blood between the staves of the Ark, according to the order of the blood of the bull: one above and seven below. And he did not intend to sprinkle neither above nor below, but rather like a whipper.

**And thus** he would count: "One. One and one. One and two. One and three. One and four. One and five. One and six. One and seven." He went out and placed it upon the second golden stand that was in the Temple hall.

**He hurried** and placed the blood of the goat, and took the blood of the bull, and sprinkled from it upon the curtain <note>separating the Holy from the Holy of Holies</note> opposite the Ark from the outside: one above and seven below. And he did not intend to sprinkle neither above nor below, but rather like a whipper.

**And thus** he would count: "One. One and one. One and two. One and three. One and four."

Specifically, when the pie <note>original: "פשטידא" (pastida)</note> is covered, it is as if the hot bread and the house are covered. And [if it] secretes [juices], and the fat of the pie drips from the bread, such that its grease does not fall beneath the bread, then Rabbi Judah bar Meir HaKohen the Elder, the teacher of Rabbenu Gershom, Light of the Exile, ruled. He used to teach him [about] a <term>alpetin</term> <gloss>a type of cooking vessel or pie dish</gloss>, and he wished to prohibit even after the fact if one baked a Gentile's pie with that of an Israelite. However, we do not hold this way. And even those who say "the aroma is not a substance" <note>original: "ריחא לאו מילתא היא"</note>, it implies that with a pie, the oven [is] such that the aroma exits from there, and if it does not hinder the bread [it is fine]. And there are those who rule like Rav <note>original: "רב"</note> in the chapter <term>Kol HaBasar</term> <gloss>All Meat</gloss> [of the Talmud], that the aroma is a substance. And the whole passage there is understood according to him, and many Geonim <note>original: "גאונים" (leaders of the Babylonian academies)</note> disagreed on the matter. And Rabbi Ibn wrote that the custom is to be careful to arrange a cover for the pie when baking them with the bread. And so too for fillings. And any cover is not as if it were like hot bread and an open house [which] Rabbenu Gershom prohibited, and even with a cover it is prohibited initially because of the vent at the top. And there are those who bake a tube of egg <note>over</note> the vent at the top so that the aroma does not exit. And Rashi <note>original: "רש"י"</note> ruled in his [commentary] that it is permitted, and the Alfasi <note>original: "האלפס" (Rabbi Isaac Alfasi)</note> also ruled that it is permitted. And even according to Rav, he only prohibited meat of a slaughtered animal and meat of an animal that died of natural causes <term>nevelah</term> <gloss>carrion</gloss>, which absorb the aroma. And similarly, hot bread and an open house that has no ventilation to the right or to the left, but only through the bung hole...

<column-break/>

[He] does not hold like Rav Kahana, that bread baked with a roast is prohibited to eat with <term>kutaḥ</term> <gloss>a spicy dip made from sour milk or whey</gloss>. But all the world is accustomed to forbid baking a pie and a salted item together. But bread with another of them is permitted. And whoever is stringent, a blessing shall come upon him. One asked him about <term>ḥameẓ</term> <gloss>leaven</gloss> and <term>maẓah</term> <gloss>unleavened bread</gloss> that were baked together in one oven, and they permitted it. And if both aromas are understood in the Talmud, the aroma of bread is not understood. And many times we bake the pie with the bread, and we found regarding the breads of the thanksgiving offering that <term>ḥameẓ</term> and <term>maẓah</term> were baked together, that no Tanna <note>rabbinic teacher of the Mishnaic period</note> skipped [mentioning] it in the traditions of two ovens, or this one or that one [were] baked [separately]. In the chapter <term>Gid HaNasheh</term> <gloss>The Sciatic Nerve</gloss> we learned regarding milk, and it is prohibited to eat even from the dish until the milk permeates, even from below to above. And we conclude that it is like this thread, and since it is like a thread it does not hinder. And even if it were to permeate a little, it is nullified. Therefore, both [the piece] that is touching it and those [where] the membrane is upon it, if there is 60 [parts of permitted food to one of forbidden], they are permitted. And there are those who say that that piece upon which the membrane is, is permitted from that which was spilled, even if it does not have 60, since the membrane is there, it is prohibited only because of the milk that is upon it from the outside, and it does not permeate beyond the membrane to the piece to which the membrane is attached. And Rabbi Simeon of Kintz said: since the kid was feduş <note>original: "פדוש" (likely referring to being salted/pitted)</note>, if it was salted, the other pieces and the roast that fell...

<column-break/>

Even though there is not 60 there. And likewise, one must judge when the milk was salted upon the pieces that do not have 60 in them. That piece is entirely prohibited. [If] it was salted, the prohibition and the permitted [meat] together, therefore, my father, the Avi HaEzri <note>original: "אבי העזרי" (Rabbi Eliezer ben Joel HaLevi)</note>, ruled: milk and meat are judged like meat [with a] peeling [required] in the place where it touched the milk, and one must deepen the peeling more than that which it was <note>if</note> one salted the meat of a lean carcass with meat into which milk was absorbed, according to [one opinion] and [one] does not say "at the time it emits it does not absorb," but rather for this reason [the] Rav and the others say the bad [meat] is suitable to absorb into its interior and will absorb. And it is not established for us that all the pieces are prohibited, and it is not sufficient with a peeling, for that which is salted is like that which is hot, for that which is roasted, for the milk permeates from the head of the kid that went out in its milk; it is prohibited to eat even from the dish... this is not [so], for it is explained regarding the kid that went out in its milk, and he eats until he reaches the milk. And he answers: that is regarding this thread, [he] eats until he reaches the milk, meaning that we can estimate until where the milk permeates according to its scarcity, for example, if the milk was abundant and was permeating and dripping, even from the ear when it was a carcass. And so Rashi explained: when we found a kidney in milk, that is what is permitted, Rabbi Yoḥanan [said]: a kidney in milk, it is permitted because the membrane separates between them. And it is not difficult for Rav, all that he prohibited even from the dish... for there the reason is because...

The person in the Holy Trinity is God the Holy Spirit, a comforter from our Lord Jesus Christ, who strengthens and comforts his faithful Christians, so that they believe in him for eternal life. So it is also with the spirit and the Matter of the Mercury <note>represented by the symbol ☿, referring here to the "mercurial" or fluidic essence of matter</note> Body: for when they come together, it is then called a doubled Mercury <term>Mercury duplicatus</term> <note>a "doubled" mercury, indicating a substance that has been joined with its own internal spirit or another metallic essence</note>, which are then two spirits: God the Father, and God the Holy Spirit; but God the Son is the Glorified Man <note>original: "Homo glorificatus"</note>, resembling our own glorified and fixed Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> of the Philosophers' Stone <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note>. Therefore this Stone is also called Threefold <note>original: "Trinus"</note>, namely originating from two Waters or Spirits, the Mineral and the Vegetable, to which an Animal Fire <note>symbol: △; the "animal" refers to the third kingdom of nature, often associated with the soul or blood</note> Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> is added. These are then two and three, and yet only one. If you do not understand this, you shall achieve nothing. Thus I have sufficiently described the Universal <note>The "Universal" refers to the Great Work or the fundamental medicine that applies to all things</note> to you through comparison: pray to God for his blessing; for without him you shall find nothing. Amen.

That I have included this reasoning from Basilius <note>Basilius Valentinus: a legendary 15th-century alchemical authority whose "Twelve Keys" are foundational to the craft</note> here, was done to prove that Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> must die just as well as the other metals. And although there are many who say that Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> cannot die, nevertheless Basilius here informs us that Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> dies through the Mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> of the Philosophers; and that this Fire <note>symbol: △</note> and Water <note>symbol: ▽</note> open the Gold and cause it to die. Want alhoewel de meeste niet nalaatig zijn, om deze Riviere tot een eynd-pale van Judéa te maaken, vertoonenze egter de zelve zoo wijd en geheel op zig-zelven voortkoomende, datze niemand tot een Arm van den Nyl, ooyt heeft konnen aanmerken. Beter heeft het misschien Strabo aangewezen, welke boven de groote Peluziaanze uytloop der Nyl, een kleynder Riviere by den Berg Kafius maakt; als waar toe hy ook de Land-Paale van Judéa, met veel andere Schrijvers uyt-rekt. Zijnde egter zoo heel-wijd niet van Rhinokorrura afgelegen, welke Stadt zoo genoemd is, na d'afgeknotte Neuzen der Burgers. Hierom moet het niemand vreemd dunken, dat in ons Land-Tafereel, hier omtrent, een kleene verandering bespeurd word. En schoon deze Riviere zoo kleyn is, datze slegts de Naam van een *Beke* verdiend, en zelfs niet met eenige Scheep-tuygen bevaarbaar is geweest; moet het ons geen wonder doen, wanneer de H. Wat nu verder den Nyl-stroom zelfs belangd, daar van zullen wy op een andere plaatze ruymer spreken.

translation:
<meta>This page continues the investigation into the precise geographical boundaries of the land promised to Abraham, specifically addressing the southwestern border at the "River of Egypt" and comparing biblical descriptions with historical and linguistic evidence.</meta>

# HISTORY OF THE HEBREW CHURCH. Chapter V.

<margin>
* See also our marginal commentators on Joshua 13:3.
</margin>

<margin>
The Nile and Sichor both named for their black color.
</margin>

<margin>
And how this river on the side of Egypt or the Southwest forms the boundaries of Canaan. And why it is slightly changed in our small map. *
</margin>

...to determine the boundaries; but also even from the name of the river *Sichor*: for just as *Sichor* <note>original Hebrew: שִׁיחוֹר (Shihor), meaning black or dark</note> means "blackish," it is generally testified that the Nile stream has blackish water; so that it is the same as if one said, *The Black River*: just as here with us, it is still called the *Swarte Water* <note>The Zwarte Water (Black Water) is a river in the Netherlands; the author uses this local comparison to help his Dutch readers understand the naming convention.</note>. Likewise the Greeks, according to Plutarchus and Eustathius, also called this river *Melas* <note>Greek: Μέλας, meaning black.</note>, and the Latins *Melo*, after its black color. Scaliger <note>Joseph Justus Scaliger (1540–1609), a renowned Dutch scholar of history and chronology.</note> also derived the word *Sirin*, with which the Ethiopians name the Nile, from the Hebrew word *Sichor*; as has been noted elsewhere in the *Jewish Antiquities*. In such a way that one must at least likely conclude that *Nahal* <note>Hebrew for "brook" or "valley river."</note> and *Sichor* here do not mean the Nile any further than that we should understand by them merely an arm of that great river which flows out at Rhinokorrura <note>A coastal town between Egypt and Palestine, modern-day El Arish.</note>. Thus all the maps in the magnificent atlases and the Bible maps are deficient in this regard and need to be corrected. For although most are not negligent in making this river a boundary of Judea, they nevertheless show it so wide and emerging entirely on its own that no one could ever have considered it an arm of the Nile. Perhaps Strabo <note>A Greek geographer from the 1st century BCE/CE.</note> indicated it better, who, above the great Pelusian mouth of the Nile, places a smaller river by Mount Casius; to which he, along with many other writers, extends the boundary of Judea. Being, however, not so very far from Rhinokorrura, which city was so named after the truncated noses of its citizens <note>The name Rhinokorrura comes from the Greek for "cut-off noses," referring to a legend that the city was a penal colony for criminals whose noses had been mutilated.</note>. Therefore, it should seem strange to no one that a small change is perceived in our map in this vicinity. And although this river is so small that it only deserves the name of a *brook* and was not even navigable by any vessels, it should not surprise us when Holy Scripture calls it the *River of Egypt* and *Sichor*, as if it intended to signify the great bosom of the Nile itself thereby; since it is very common that in things of the same kind, especially water, the name of the whole is also given to its part. As for what further concerns the Nile stream itself, we shall speak more extensively of that in another place.

<margin>
Boundaries of Canaan indicated to the North and Northeast.
</margin>

<margin>
Whether Abraham's descendants ever possessed the Land of Canaan in the extent promised, namely from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates or the Great River.
</margin>

If we have then correctly found the divine boundary of Canaan to the South or Southwest against Egypt, we have no more difficulty remaining in discovering the same to the North or Northeast at the Euphrates, which Moses, not unjustly, calls *The Great River*. As to which our map sufficiently indicates the situation of its course; already described enough by us previously. But there another dispute arises to be brought from black darkness into the light: namely, how and where one shall correctly place the fulfillment of the promise in this wide region of the land? Since not only did the Jews never have all the provinces situated between these two rivers—the Nile and the Euphrates—in hereditary possession (which is nevertheless promised in plain words); but also, in Numbers 34, the possession of the land is not given to Israel further than *Hamath*, which is truly still very far on this side of the Euphrates. But let us hear the opinions of the scholars and then choose which one we wish to support. Jerome <note>original: Hieronymus, the 4th-century Church Father who translated the Vulgate.</note>, and after him Masius <note>Andreas Masius (1514–1573), a Flemish priest and humanist scholar of the Near East.</note> with others, are of the opinion that the promise of such a broad possession of the land was made under the condition of a laudable obedience on the part of Abraham's seed, that is *Israel*: which not having been proven by them later, God was released from His word of promise and was not bound to fulfill it to the end. To which one might remark that if the promise was made under condition, such an implicit condition must then rather apply to the whole promise and not only to certain parts of it...

It also introduces a theological debate regarding why the Israelites never fully occupied the vast territory between the Nile and the Euphrates as promised to Abraham.</summary>

<meta>Commentary on the Jialiang standard measure of the Zhou and Han dynasties, comparing ancient and modern units.</meta>
Note: of both the Zhou <term>fu</term> <gloss>cauldron-shaped standard measure</gloss> and the Han <term>hu</term> <gloss>standard grain measure of ten dou</gloss> it is said that they are one <term>chi</term> <gloss>foot</gloss> deep, one chi square on the inside, and round on the outside. Their stated dimensions are the same, yet their capacities differ. Earlier scholars therefore all bent the facts to fit an explanation. On examination, what they call "one chi square" is really more than one chi square, which is why it is said that "there is a margin at the sides" <note>original: "旁有庇焉", a phrase from the classical description of the vessel, meaning the circle extends beyond the inscribed square</note>. So those measurements were never a fixed standard either. Here we use the <term>lüchi</term> <gloss>pitch-pipe foot, the ancient foot derived from the pitch pipes</gloss> to derive capacity, and the <term>yingzao chi</term> <gloss>builder's foot, the standard foot of the Ming and Qing</gloss> to state the dimensions. In this way the agreement and difference between ancient and modern length, capacity and weight can be seen clearly. translation:
<meta>continues from previous page: "My Note"</meta>to answer to "never indulging." But on reflection, "not harming its straightness" refers back to the straightness of "nourishing with straightness" above, and should not be tied only to "never indulging." ○ From this point the text begins afresh, interweaving two ideas, "never casting away, never indulging" and "able to endure, able to be great." Both are ways of fully realizing the Way of Heaven and Earth and resembling it. This section shares its meaning with the section beginning "The clear are different things," and the "When the will is great" section shares its meaning with the three sections beginning "metal and harmony." <note>These refer to other passages in Zhang Zai's text; the exact sections are not identified here.</note>

When the will is great, talent is great and undertakings are great; therefore it says "able to be great," and also "rich possession." When the will endures, one's <term>qi</term> <gloss>vital energy</gloss> endures and one's virtuous nature endures; therefore it says "able to endure," and also "daily renewal."

**Cited Source:** The *Book of Changes*, "Great Commentary, Part One," chapter 1: "Having intimacy, it can endure; having achievement, it can be great. Being able to endure is the virtue of the worthy; being able to be great is the enterprise of the worthy." Chapter 5: "Rich possession is called the great enterprise."

### Twenty-fifth day. Clear.
The <term>Crown Prince</term> was at the <term>Shenyang Residence</term>. He granted an audience to the high officials <term>Park Ro</term> and <term>Park Hwang</term>, and the <term>Literary Official</term> <term>Jeong Noe-gyeong</term>.

### Twenty-sixth day. Clear.
The <term>Crown Prince</term> was at the <term>Shenyang Residence</term>. <term>Generals Long and Ma</term> <gloss>Inggūldai and Mafuta</gloss> summoned <term>Park Ro</term> to their government office. They questioned him about the marriage of court ladies, the status of those who had surrendered to the Qing, and the return of defectors. They scolded him for not carrying these matters out quickly. <term>Park Ro</term> endured the verbal abuse. The generals then became angry over the violation of the ban on tobacco. <term>Park Ro</term> returned and reported their angry words. The Prince immediately called for <term>Park Ro</term> to hear the full conversation. <term>Park Ro</term> entered and attended. Soon after, the two generals summoned <term>Park Ro</term> again to the <term>West Residence</term>. <gloss>At that time, a large amount of tobacco was searched and discovered in the luggage of Eunuch Han Yeo-gi. It was piled in the courtyard and set on fire. All tobacco, whether public or private, was burned, and not a single leaf remained.</gloss> <term>Park Ro</term> returned and was called in again to explain the details of the situation. <term>Min Eung-hyeop</term>, the <term>Pilsun</term> <gloss>Tutor to the Crown Prince</gloss>, entered to attend.

### Twenty-seventh day. Clear.
The <term>Crown Prince</term> was at the <term>Shenyang Residence</term>. <term>Eunuch</term> <term>Han Yeo-gi</term> was dismissed from his post and forced to return home by horse.

右南康軍治舊堂記。樂城徐君師田。壁堂作。手書而刻石焉。自元豐乙丑。距今淳熙己亥。凡九十有五年。而新安朱熹。未領郡事。向堂所在。則既多有。而杉亦不存。求其記文。則又非復故刻。而委之它所矣。於是悉訪郡之老。人竟無有能言其處者。蓋自元豐以至今。其間世故亦多憂矣。兵連建炎。群盜亦今終。十年舊迹。盡滅未應。且再意者。斯堂之毀。其在絕壑黨亂之時乎。撫事興懷。慨然永歎。顧郡方貧。而民已病。便堂之役。基尚在。勢亦不能有復作其舊。獨廳事之面。有堂。妄額而產中有老柏焉。焚薪之餘。生意殆盡。而屹立不傷。如志士仁人。更歷憂患。而剝毅獨立。凜然不衰者。因取直。節之。辦寓之斯堂。而筆記石壁間。且欲盡去庭之厄。而雜植杉柏。以待前賢之遺意。則既非時。而熹亦以病告歸矣。嗚呼。遂君子其尚有以成予之志也。夫是歲。分丁亥歲。

行藏動業。銷倚樓。看鏡之懷。窮寇崎嶇。增尋壑徑之趣。此老子心事也。公方欲求試南宮。希輒。自與何哉。然予心濡滯。於此而未得遂。其所懷也。三復其言。為之太息。庚子至前一日。六老軒書。

跋南上人詩
南上人此卷。求余舊詩。而坐為寫。此及遠遊秋夜等篇。顧念山林。俯仰晴昔。為之慨然。南詩清嚴。有餘格力。閒暇絕無疏筍氣。如去沾衣。濕杏花雨。吹面不寒。楊柳風。余深愛之。不知世人以為何也。淳熙辛丑。清明晦。翁書。

跋穎魯公栗里詩
右唐魯郡顏文忠公栗里詩。見陳令舉。廬山記。而不得其全篇。雖欲讀之者。亦足以識公之心。而著於君臣。

translation:
On the right is a record of the old hall of the Nankang military administration. It was written and carved on stone by Xu Shitian of Lecheng. From the <term>Yi-Chou</term> year of <term>Yuanfeng</term> <gloss>1085</gloss> to the present <term>Ji-Hai</term> year of <term>Chunxi</term> <gloss>1179</gloss>, a total of ninety-five years have passed. Before I, Zhu Xi of Xin’an, took charge of the prefecture's affairs, the places where the hall used to be were many, but the cedars no longer survived. When I sought the text of the record, it was no longer the original carving but had been moved elsewhere. Thereupon, I visited all the elders of the prefecture, but in the end, no one could say where its location was. From the <term>Yuanfeng</term> era to now, many world events have caused sorrow. War continued into the <term>Jianyan</term> era, and bands of thieves only recently ceased. After ten years, the old traces have completely vanished. I suspect the destruction of this hall occurred during the time of turmoil in the remote valleys. Reflecting on these events, I sigh deeply. Seeing that the prefecture is currently poor and the people are already suffering, even though the foundation for the hall work remains, the situation does not allow for it to be rebuilt as it was. However, facing the government office, there is a hall with a plaque, and in the courtyard stands an old cypress tree. Despite the remains of burnt wood around it, its life force is nearly exhausted, yet it stands tall and unharmed. It is like a man of high purpose and benevolence who has passed through many troubles, standing independent and firm, solemn and unyielding. Therefore, I took its upright character and placed it in this hall, recording it on the stone wall. I also wished to remove all the obstructions from the courtyard and plant cedars and cypresses to honor the remaining intentions of former worthies. But the time was not right, and I have submitted my resignation due to illness. Alas! May later gentlemen still fulfill my ambition. This was the <term>Ding-Hai</term> year <gloss>1167</gloss>.

### Postscript to the Brief Biography of Zhang Keming

The choice to serve or retire, and one's active achievements, fade like the feeling of leaning on a balcony and looking into a mirror. The winding paths of a cornered foe increase the interest in seeking a valley path. This is the state of mind of the old masters. You are about to seek examination in the Southern Palace; why do you suddenly follow your own path? Yet my heart is delayed here and has not yet been able to fulfill its desires. I have read your words three times and sighed for them. Written at the Six Elders Studio on the day before the <term>Geng-Zi</term> solstice.

### Postscript to the Poems of Monk Nan

In this scroll, Monk Nan asked for my old poems, so I sat and wrote these, along with "Far Travels" and "Autumn Night." Thinking of the mountains and forests, looking up and down at the past and present, I feel deeply moved. Nan's poetry is clear and strict, with ample strength and character. In his leisure, he has absolutely no trace of the "coarseness of a monk." It is like rain that wets apricot blossoms without drenching one's clothes, or a willow wind that blows on the face without being cold. I love it deeply; I do not know what the rest of the world thinks of it. On the last day of the Qingming festival in the <term>Xin-Chou</term> year of <term>Chunxi</term> <gloss>1181</gloss>, written by the Old Man.

### Postscript to the "Lili" Poem by Yan Ying Lu Gong

On the right is the "Lili" poem by Yan Wenzhong Gong <note>Yan Zhenqing</note> of Lu Commandery. I saw it in Chen Lingju’s *Record of Mount Lu*, but it was not the complete poem. Even so, for those who wish to read it, it is enough to recognize the Duke’s heart and his dedication to the righteousness of lord and minister.

He once said, "I received the *Great Learning* and the *Analects* from my late father. I only learned the punctuation. After several years, I suddenly lamented that my father and elder brother had passed away and there was no one to encourage me. How could I establish myself? So I searched through the books in the house and found a tattered copy of the *Doctrine of the Mean*. I sat upright and read it along with the small annotations, continuing through day and night. Once I was familiar with the pronunciations and sounds of the characters, I searched for the meaning of each word. Once the word meanings were clear, I searched for the meaning of the sentences. Then I expanded this to the meaning of chapters and the entire book. As the months and years passed, I became saturated and soaked in the text. I could not bear to put it into practice until it became suddenly clear and manifest. After I had a thoroughly pleasant understanding, I moved on to the *Great Learning*, the *Analects*, and the *Mencius*, as if I were meeting old friends." <margin>In the year of Eul-myo.</margin> Even when he was the Head of the Office of Special Advisors, he still acted like a young scholar, focusing on encouragement without any intention of personal gain. The lion <note>Pingalaka</note> clawed the back of Sanjivaka <gloss>the bull</gloss> with his lotus-like nails, and the bull struck the lion's belly and face with his horns. Again and again, a great battle took place between them, filled with enmity and wrath.

Seeing both of them with their sides and faces covered in blood, Karataka said to Damanaka with reproach: "Fie! Everything is ruined by your littleness of mind.

Those ministers are truly skilled in policy who bring about affairs through affection, which otherwise would require thousands of difficult states. Those who, possessing little wealth, desire fruitless results through wicked efforts, bring the face of Fortune <note>term: Shri</note> into the mouth of a lion through their bad conduct." <note>Verse 136</note>

Therefore, you fool:
A man who knows his business should first employ conciliation. Methods accomplished through conciliation do not lead to defeat. <note>Verse 137</note>

The darkness born of hatred is not overcome by a polished jewel, nor by the sun, nor by fire, but through conciliation. <note>Verse 138</note>

Policy is seen to be fourfold, starting with conciliation <note>term: sama</note> and ending with force <note>term: danda</note>. Among these, force is the most sinful; therefore, one should avoid it. <note>Verse 139</note>

Through conciliation, gifts, and sowing dissension, one may attain wealth, a kingdom, or a wife. But he who understands the four means knows when to use human effort. <note>Verse 140</note>

Order according to the scriptures is eternal, and the means should follow the proper order. When a beginning is made with the right means, success follows the beginning. <note>Verse 141</note>

Even with the strength of two means, if an affair is conducted perversely, it leaves the path of virtue and policy is broken. <note>Verse 142</note>

Force should only be used as a last resort, just as poison is used by a physician when other medicines fail. <note>Verse 143</note>

Many heroes have set out, powerful in their speech and deeds, but even those with eyes are blind if they do not follow wisdom. <note>Verse 144</note>

Even if you think, "I am a minister's son," you have gone to a place of ruin. That too is for your own destruction.
Whether he is not constrained by hardship, or does not exist in the nature of the great, or does not act according to the law, or does not follow the words of the gods: if a man has no peace or wisdom, then what is he? <note>Verse 145</note>

<summary>Karataka severely rebukes Damanaka for inciting a violent conflict between the lion and the bull, citing the principles of political science that favor conciliation over force.</summary>

While the previous page focused on predicting the birth of a son, this page expands the scope to identify various people in the querent's life based on the houses of the horoscope and concludes with predictions regarding travel and the nature of a man's wife or female companions.</meta>

<page-num>२५</page-num>

<margin>25</margin> The querent's village is like his own body; some things are held in the mind. From there, one should judge the work to be done. From the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: "Lagna"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, if a planet is in the third house <note>original: "Sahaja"; literally 'born together', referring to siblings</note>, one speaks of siblings. If in the fifth house, one speaks of a son or grandson. If in the fourth house, one should speak of the mother or the mother's sister <note>maternal aunt</note>. If in the sixth house, one speaks of a foe or enemy. If in the seventh house, one speaks of the wife <note>original: "Jaya"</note>, especially based on the strength of the planets residing in the seventh from the Ascendant. If in the ninth house, which is the house of <term>Dharma</term> <note>religion, duty, or the father</note>, one should speak of matters related to merit and religion. In the tenth house, one speaks of the teacher <note>original: "Guru"</note>, masters, and horses.

The lord of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>the ruler of the specific 1/9th division of the sign</note> occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant at that time determines the desire of the querent. If that lord is auspicious and well-placed, the outcome is good. If the lord of the house of enemies is situated in the Ascendant at the time of the query, then one should speak of an enemy. Now, regarding the placement of "faults" or "strengths" in the houses: among the many planets, the one that is most powerful determines the location or state of the querent’s desire. <margin>Rama</margin> Furthermore, in the same manner, by looking at the planetary strengths, one can determine if a person is surrounded by friends or if the rest are enemies, as shown in the books of <term>Jataka</term> <note>natal astrology</note>. <margin>25</margin>

Now, the knowledge regarding the "Thoughts on Travel" <note>original: "Pravasa Chinta"</note> is stated:

**Regarding the Movable Signs... || 51 ||**
When the <term>Movable Navamshas</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note> are rising in the seventh house or the Ascendant at the time of the query, one should speak of travel.

---

One should speak of the querent's travel from the <term>Navamshaka</term>. If the lord of the Ascendant is in a certain position, the person is thinking of journeying to a foreign land. Here is the specific certainty: regarding the seventh and ninth houses. From the Ascendant, if there is a planet in the seventh house that is <term>Retrograde</term> <note>original: "Vakrita"; appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, then the traveler who has gone abroad will return. If the planet is not retrograde, or if the sign in the seventh or ninth house is not occupied by a returning planet, then the person will not return.

Now, if the querent asks: "What kind of woman will I have a connection with?" that knowledge is provided:

**The Sun and others... || 52 ||**
Based on whether the Sun, Venus <note>original: "Sita"</note>, Mars <note>original: "Vakra"</note>, or Mercury <note>original: "Saumya"</note> are in the seventh house <note>the house of partnerships</note>, one predicts the woman. If the Sun is there, it may be another's wife. If Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note> is there, one should say the woman is a lawful wife. If Mercury is present, she may be a woman of the merchant class <note>original: "Vaishya"</note> or a supporter. If the Moon is there, she is a courtesan. Similarly, if Saturn <note>original: "Sora" or "Shanishchara"</note> is in the seventh house, one should say he approaches a woman from an outcaste or very ignorant family.

The age and status of these women are known from the Moon: if the Moon is in its early phase, she is a young girl; if in its middle phase, she is a youthful woman; if in its late phase, she is an elderly woman. These have been shown by the wise in previous teachings. Now, the signs of illness and the knowledge of recovery will be spoken of.

# Compendium of Essence
<note>original: "Sāra Saṃgraha"</note>

<margin>Ho · 1</margin> **Om. Salutations to the holy Lord Ganesha.** <note>Ganesha is traditionally invoked at the beginning of Hindu texts to remove obstacles.</note> Having bowed to the Lord of Obstacles [Ganesha], the Goddess Saraswati <note>the goddess of knowledge and the arts</note>, and the Guru, this **Compendium of Essence** is composed for the instruction of the young <note>original: "bāla-bodhāya," meaning "for the awakening of children" or beginners</note>.

In the year **1833** of the Vikrama Samvat era <note>approx. 1776 CE</note> and **1790** of the Shaka era <note>approx. 1868 CE; note that these dates do not align traditionally, suggesting either a later annotation or a specific regional reckoning</note>.

**Now follow the months:**
Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashvina, Kartika, Margashira, Pausha, Magha, and Phalguna—12 months in total.

**Now the fortnights:**
The dark half <note>original: "krishna-paksha," the waning moon</note> and the light half <note>original: "shukla-paksha," the waxing moon</note>.

**Now the lunar days:** <note>term: "tithi" — the 30 divisions of the lunar month</note>
The first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth, and fourteenth days; then the Full Moon <note>original: "purnima"</note> and the New Moon <note>original: "amavasya"</note>.

**Now the days of the week:**
Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday—7 days.

**Now the lunar mansions:** <note>term: "nakshatra" — the 28 sectors of the ecliptic through which the moon passes</note>
1. Ashvini, 2. Bharani, 3. Krittika, 4. Rohini, 5. Mrigashira, 6. Ardra, 7. Punarvasu, 8. Pushya, 9. Ashlesha, 10. Magha, 11. Purva-Phalguni, 12. Uttara-Phalguni, 13. Hasta, 14. Chitra, 15. Svati, 16. Vishakha, 17. Anuradha, 18. Jyeshtha, 19. Mula, 20. Purva-Ashadha, 21. Uttara-Ashadha, 22. Abhijit, 23. Shravana, 24. Dhanishtha, 25. Shatabhisha, 26. Purva-Bhadrapada, 27. Uttara-Bhadrapada, 28. Revati.

**Now the zodiac signs:** <note>term: "rashi" — the twelve signs of the solar zodiac</note>
Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces—12 signs.

**[Phonetic Table for Naming]**
<note>This section maps specific sounds to the "quarters" of each lunar mansion to determine auspicious names for children born at those times.</note>
*Chu, Che, Cho, La* for **Ashvini**;
*Li, Lu, Le, Lo* for **Bharani**;
*A, I, U, E* for **Krittika**;
*O, Va, Vi, Vu* for **Rohini**;
*Ve, Vo, Ka, Ki* for **Mrigashira**;
*Ku, Gha, Nga, Cha* for **Ardra**;
*Ke, Ko, Ha, Hi* for **Punarvasu**;
*Hu, He, Ho, Da* for **Pushya**;
*Di, Du, De, Do* for **Ashlesha**;
*Ma, Mi, Mu, Me* for **Magha**;
*Mo, Ti, Tu, Te* for **Purva-Phalguni**;
*Te, To, Pa, Pi* for **Uttara-Phalguni**;
*E, Sha, Na, Tha* for **Hasta**;
*Pe, Po, Ra, Ri* for **Chitra**...

<margin>3</margin>

Degrees are subtracted from the <term>Solar Transit<note>original: "Saṃkrānti"; the moment the Sun moves from one zodiac sign to another.</note></term> day to determine the positions. Earth (1), eyes (2), fire (3), flavors (6), serpents (8), time (9), water (10), king (11), and song (12). Thus ends the **Five-fold Mercury** calculation. ॥ 

If Mercury is in an odd sign while the Sun is in an odd sign relative to the Moon, and the Sun is in an odd sign relative to Mercury, then this is known as <term>Ekārgala<note>original: "Ekārgala"; literally 'a single bolt,' referring to a specific obstructive astrological configuration that acts as a 'bolt' against success.</note></term>. It is to be avoided in all auspicious works. Thus ends the **Ekārgala** section. ॥ 7 ॥

During the night, the <term>Secondary Planets<note>original: "Upagrahāḥ"; calculated mathematical points or "shadow planets" that influence the chart, often negatively.</note></term> are counted as follows: Bird (5), Indra (14), six (10), nine-Moon (18), day-chaff (22), three-feet (23), and the wheel-maker (25), counted from the Sun. Thus ends the section on **Secondary Planets**. ॥ 10 ॥

The <term>Equality of Declination<note>original: "Kāntisāmyaṃ"; a period when the Sun and Moon have the same declination, considered highly inauspicious.</note></term> is known from the Sun's position: five (5), three (3), ten (10), twenty-four (27), sixty-eight (8), sky-direction (10), etc. <note>The text here uses a complex numerical code to map specific planetary degrees.</note> Seven, four, three, one, eight, four, eleven, seventeen, six, twelve, and three; equality is reached when the Sun and Moon are in the same or opposite signs. Thus ends the section on **Equality of Declination**.

Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, <insert>and</insert> Libra, <unclear>Scorpio</unclear>, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces.
The six, four, eight, six, ten, eight, two, one, two, twelve, and pairs of wealth—these signs are <term>Burned<note>original: "Dagdhāḥ"; specific signs or days that are considered 'incinerated' or void of power during certain solar months.</note></term>. Thus ends the **Burned Signs** section.

Regarding the <term>Ascendants<note>original: "Lagna"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific time.</note></term> during day and night, some say the twilight hour is without defect. For Leo, Virgo, Capricorn, and Sagittarius, the calculation begins from Aries and follows the pairs. Thus ends the **Ascendants for Twilight** and other times.

When the Moon is in the 2nd, 3rd, or 11th house from the Ascendant, it is called <term>The Hour of Cow-Dust<note>original: "Godhūli"; the period of sunset when returning cattle kick up dust. In Indian astrology, this is often a 'safety valve' time when many minor astrological defects are neutralized.</note></term>, provided there is no <unclear>cruel</unclear> planet or Equality of Declination. Some say the 4th house from Mars and others. Thus ends the **Hour of Cow-Dust**.

If the Sun is in the Ascendant's <term>half-sign<note>original: "Horā"</note></term>, or the Moon is in its own, or if the day-lord is Mercury or Jupiter, marriage does not lead to death. Cruel planets in the center cause suffering to the body. Thus ends the section on **Planetary Afflictions**. Benefic planets in the <term>Quadrants<note>original: "Kendra"</note></term> remove defects. All planets in the 11th (Rudra) or 9th (Dhananjaya) houses, or malefic planets in the 6th, 11th, or 3rd houses, create a favorable <term>Line of Fortune<note>original: "Rekha"</note></term>. Thus ends the **Planetary Lines**. Calculation of the lineage, wealth, and the <term>Kulikā<note>original: "Kulikā"; a specific portion of the day ruled by a 'shadow' planet, usually considered unlucky.</note></term> period in order. Thus ends the **Kulikā** section.

**Thus concludes the Jewel-Message of Marriage, composed by the illustrious Hemakara.** ॥ 2863 ॥

He possesses a **distinctive appearance** <note>original: "svasvarūpaḥ"; implies a form that is characteristic or true to his own nature</note>. He has **prominent cheekbones**, a **high nose**, and a **round forehead**. He is **full of desire** <note>original: "kāmābhilāṣī"; referring to a sensual or passionate temperament</note>. He is **prosperous**, with wealth that seems to gather in the "lotus-base" of his face <note>original: "mukhe kamalatale vadhadhanaḥ"; an idiomatic way of saying his prosperity is evident in his countenance or speech</note>.

His constitution is governed by the **Vata and Kapha humors** <term>vata-śleshma</term> <note>the biological energies of "wind" and "phlegm" in Ayurvedic medicine, often resulting in a frame that is either very lean or prone to steadiness and cool temperament</note>. He is **inclined toward laziness**. He is a **devotee of his teacher, the gods, and the sacred fire**.

He is **fair-complexioned** and **resolute** in nature. At the time of birth, he is as small as a **Raktika seed** <note>original: "rattikā samāḥ"; the Raktika or Gunja seed was a traditional unit of weight; this likely refers to a specific physical measurement or a birthmark</note>. He has **prominent veins** <note>original: "vāyavī-śirāḥ"; literally "wind-veins," a physical trait often associated with the Vata constitution</note> and is **endowed with auspicious lines on the soles of his feet**. He is **fond of royal assemblies** <note>original: "rājasabhā-priyaḥ"; suggests he enjoys the company of high society or political circles</note>. He is one who **subsists on milk** <note>original: "kṣīrabhojī"; implies a refined, pure, or "Sattvic" diet</note>, and he is **exceptionally fortunate**.

# Hertochdom Milanen.

Dit Hertochdom wordt voor het befte Hertochdom der geheelder Chriftenheyt gheacht, ghelijck Vlaenderen het befte Graeffchap; ghelijck wij te dyer plaetfen ghefeyt hebben. Het is een feer coftelyck ende vruchtbaer landt (gelijck om fegghen geheel Lombardyen is, daert een deel af is), de principael ftadt daer in is Milanen, daer 't hertochdom finen naem na heeft. Defe ftadt is feer vermaert ende beker-it geworden deur de oorlogen in onfen tijden, dier tuffchen den Keyfer Carolus de vijfde, en Francifcus de eerfte van dyen naeme Coninck van Vranckrijck om gevoert fijn geweeft; ende oock deur haer Cafteel datter aen leet, dwelck onder alle fterckten der Chriftenheyt eenē grootē naem heeft. Men telt defe ftadt voor eene vande grootfte fteden van Europa: ende fal oock wel metter tijt de ftercfte beeten, waren de mueren ende bolwercken rontsomme volmaect, daer wij An. 1559. aen fagen wercken. Hoewel dat defe ftadt foo groot is ende naer advenant vol volcks, foo is te verwonderen datter de lijfneeringe foo goeden coop is; maer dat maeckt het vruchtbaer aertrijck daerfe in ghelegen is, ende foo veel wateren ende beken daerfe rontsom van wt het gheberchte en de groote Riviere Po mede gedient wordt; waer deur alle dingen die den menfche nootelyck fijn, oft tot vermaeck ende luft begheert worden, overvloedelyck ende goeden coop, ghebracht worden. Soo groote menichte van alderleye Cunften en hantwercken fijn hier, dattet nauwelyck te gelooven en is; alfoo dat in Italien een fpreecwoort is, Wie Italien beteren wilde, moefte Milanen verderven; te weten, dat hun alfoo de Cunftenaren ende wercklieden hier wt verjaecht fijnde, deur geheel Italien ftroyen ende verbreyden fouden. Seer veel coftelycke ende treffelycke edificien ende ghebouwen fijnder, onder de welcke de principaelste is de opperfte Kercke den Dom gheheeten, waer aen de Cunfte met de Coftelyckheyt fchijnen om prijs te vechten. Ick hebbe fomtijts ghefeyt dattet my dochte een Bagge te fyne, om datfe van onder tot boven met Marmoren beelden, ende alderley ander cieraet ende gefnedenwerck foo overvloedelyck van buyten becleet is, datfe fchijnt niet van Steenbouders, maer van Siluerfmeden gemaect te fyne. De andere Kercken ende Heeren-huyfen fouden hier te lanck fijn te befchryven. Maer die een Burgers oft priuaet perfoons huys wil fien, die gae te Milanen ende vraghe nae het huys dat Tomas de Marini Genewois daer heeft laten maken, (ick dencke dattet nu voldaen is) ende dat van buyten en van binnen wel deur fien hebbende, mach hy hem wel voor laten ftaen, algaet hy verde dat hi nerghens gheen coftelycker oft mogelyck diefghelycx fien en fal. Dit meyne ick dat met my fegghen fullen, alle die haer fulcx verftaende, landen ende Steden befocht hebben. Andere fteden onder dit Hertochdom gheleghen, fijn Pauia feer vermaert deur de hooghe fchole dyer is, ende den flach die fynen onfterffelycken naem van haer heeft, ende by haer ghefchiede An. 1525. daer in Francifcus de Coninck van Vranckrijck ghevangen werdt; daer nae Crema, Lodi certijts Laus Pompeia gheheeten, Como van ghelegentheyt feer playfant, ghelijck wij op haer plaetfe fegghen fullen, ende andere.

# Duchy of Milan.

This Duchy is considered the best Duchy of all Christendom, just as Flanders is the best County; as we have said in those places. It is a very precious and fertile land (as is indeed the whole of Lombardy, of which it is a part); the principal city therein is Milan, from which the Duchy has its name. This city is very famous and has become well-known through the wars in our times, which were waged between the Emperor Charles the Fifth and Francis the First of that name, King of France; and also through its Castle that lies there, which has a great name among all the fortresses of Christendom. One counts this city as one of the largest cities of Europe: and it will also likely in time be the strongest, were the walls and bastions round about completed, on which we saw work being done in the year 1559. Although this city is so large and proportionally full of people, it is still to be wondered at that food is so cheap there; but that is caused by the fertile soil in which it is situated, and so many waters and streams with which it is surrounded and served from the mountains and the great river Po; through which all things that are necessary for man, or desired for pleasure and delight, are brought in abundantly and at a good price. So great a multitude of all kinds of arts and crafts are here, that it is hardly to be believed; so that there is a proverb in Italy: "He who would improve Italy, must destroy Milan"; meaning that the artists and workmen, being chased out of here, would scatter and spread through all of Italy. There are very many precious and excellent edifices and buildings, among which the most principal is the supreme church, called the <term>Dom</term> <gloss>Cathedral</gloss>, where art and costliness seem to fight for the prize. I have sometimes said that it seemed to me to be a trinket, because it is so abundantly covered from bottom to top with marble statues and all kinds of other ornament and carved work on the outside, that it seems to be made not by stonemasons, but by silversmiths. The other churches and noble houses would be too long to describe here. But he who wants to see a citizen's or private person's house, let him go to Milan and ask for the house that Tomas de Marini, a Genoese, has had made there (I think it is now finished), and having seen it well through from outside and inside, he may well boast to himself, even if he travels far, that he will nowhere see anything more precious or possibly like it. This I think all who have visited lands and cities with such understanding will say with me. Other cities situated under this Duchy are Pavia, very famous through the university that is there, and the battle that has its immortal name from it, and happened near it in the year 1525, where Francis, the King of France, was captured; thereafter Crema, Lodi, formerly called <term>Laus Pompeia</term> <gloss>the Roman name for Lodi</gloss>, Como, very pleasant in its situation, as we shall say in its place, and others.

<margin>King of Narfinga on a pilgrimage.</margin>
a day's journey from there in a <term>pagoda</term> <gloss>temple</gloss>, where he had come on a pilgrimage with much gold and silver for the healing of an illness with which he was afflicted. The reason for this flight of Timoja was that some of his friends had let him know that the King wanted to have him taken prisoner, due to some complaints that had been made against him because he had taken several ships at sea as a <term>sea-rover</term> <gloss>pirate</gloss>. The Viceroy, meanwhile continuing his journey, came to Cananor, where he was received with very great splendor, and during the 3 days he stayed there, there was nothing but joy and exuberance throughout the entire city.
